title: Laser treatment for glaucoma
what: The doctor uses a laser to help fluid drain out of the eye better. This lowers the pressure in the eye.
why: For glaucoma or high eye pressure, and for a narrow drainage angle, to prevent an attack.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 5 to 15 minutes, about an hour with preparation
tell_doctor: Heart and lung conditions. Some drops affect them

prepare.title: Drops
prepare.text: Do not stop your glaucoma drops on your own. Ask your doctor whether to use them that day.

prepare.title: Getting there
prepare.text: Vision may be blurry afterward. Best to come with someone.

steps: The eye is numbed with drops, sometimes the pupil is narrowed or widened
You sit at the machine with your chin on a stand
A lens is placed on your eye
The doctor gives laser pulses, and you see flashes
After a while, your eye pressure is checked
feel: Blurry vision for a few hours
after: Use the prescribed drops, and your own drops as your doctor says
Come for pressure checks on time
The laser's effect is judged after a few weeks
red_flags: Severe eye pain, headache, nausea, or rainbow rings around lights: call emergency services or see an eye doctor urgently

faq.q: Can I stop my drops after the laser?
faq.a: Sometimes you need fewer drops, but only your doctor decides.
Glaucoma is lifelong. The laser helps keep the pressure normal.

faq.q: Will it need to be repeated?
faq.a: Sometimes the effect fades over time, and it is repeated.

reminders.text: Glaucoma laser tomorrow. Bring your eye drops and sunglasses.
